asis-q4-r3.review_only: The numbers below are checked against the paper notes.
asis-q4-r3.comment: Every number I checked matches the papers: Mem0 Table 2 (72.90 vs 66.88, p95 1.440 s vs 17.117 s), Mem0 §4.5 p. 14 (7k vs 600k tokens), Zep Table 2 p. 7 (71.2% vs 60.2%, 1.6k vs 115k), MemoryAgentBench Table 3 (60.6 / 21.1 / 24.0 / 28.3, memory agents on GPT-4o-mini), HaluMem p. 11 (all but MemOS under 60% recall). Only 4 papers carry page links (Mem0, Zep, MemoryAgentBench, HaluMem); the other 19 are named in the family table. Points 3, 4 and 5 are only gestured at ('everything is kept', 'the model itself', 'a usage score'), so not counted; point 12 is counted for the axis, without the Memory-R1 figure. It misses the functional split, the independent 12-system study (points 16-21), forgetting (28-29) and EvoMemBench. Not checked: 'eight families' and the 'same system moves by more than the claimed margins' claim, which come from the review.

errors.quote: Rethinking Memory in LLM-based Agents for the write/manage/read loop
errors.paper_says: The write–manage–read loop is from 'Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents: Mechanisms, Evaluation, and Emerging Frontiers' (abstract and Contributions: 'We formalize agent memory as a write–manage–read loop'). 'Rethinking Memory in LLM based Agents' never uses the phrase; it organises memory into parametric and contextual forms and six atomic operations.

errors.quote: Both put 1–3K tokens in the prompt.
errors.paper_says: Minor. In Mem0's Table 2, the same paper that gives the 7K and 600K store sizes, Zep's retrieved context is 3,911 tokens and Mem0's is 1,764. Zep is in the 1–3K range only in its own LongMemEval run (1.6k, Zep Table 2, p. 7).

asis+claude-sonnet-5-5-q4-r1.review_only: I took this from the review alone and didn't open the individual papers, so treat the numbers as the review's.
asis+claude-sonnet-5-5-q4-r1.misleading: Mildly. It files A-MEM, LightMem and SeCom under 'one memory is an LLM-extracted fact', although SeCom stores topical segments and A-MEM linked notes. 'Graphs aren't a good default' leans on AgentMemBench, whose graph strategy is a spaCy triple extractor (p. 6), not Zep or HippoRAG. It gives no page references, so nothing can be looked up.
asis+claude-sonnet-5-5-q4-r1.comment: No page citations or links; 33 papers are named, none located. The numbers it does give hold: 7K vs 600K (Mem0 p. 14), 44.4 vs 15.6 (Are We Ready Table 2), 7–9.5% (ForgetEval Limitations and Appendix N), under 60% recall (HaluMem p. 11), and AgentMemBench graph Recall@5 of 0.001 on LoCoMo (p. 10). The five design questions are a useful frame and cover point 12 and point 14 (including LightMem's idle-time work). No mechanism is explained beyond one table cell, and it ends by offering to do the checking it did not do.

errors.quote: Experiential memory is best on tool-use execution
errors.paper_says: True only within an episode. EvoMemBench Finding 4 (p. 7) has procedural methods (ReasoningBank, AWM) strongest on in-episode execution. Finding 7 (p. 8), in the cited range, says that across episodes 'In Tool Using, retrieval-augmented memory achieves the best family-level average rank' (5.43); procedural memory is best only in Embodied AI.

errors.quote: ReasoningBank distils up to three strategy items per finished task ... ([ReasoningBank, p. 4]
errors.paper_says: Minor page error. §3.2 on p. 4 says only 'we extract multiple memory items for each trajectory' and defers to Appendix A.1; the limit ('at most three memory items') is in Appendix A.1, p. 21. The failures-and-successes and append-only parts are on p. 4.

noreviews-q4-r1.review_only: I worked from the library's notes on 17 of the 42 agent papers and 5 of the 10 benchmarks; the rest, including MemOS, MIRIX, HippoRAG, ExpeL and Agent Workflow Memory, are placed by their one-line index summaries only.
noreviews-q4-r1.comment: The strongest answer: it explains mechanisms with a running example and is the only one to use the independent 12-system study. 11 papers carry page links, and they check out: MemGPT memory pressure (§2.2, p. 2), MemoryOS heat (p. 4–5), Generative Agents (p. 8–9), SeCom Table 1 (p. 6), Mem0 (p. 3–4, Table 2), Zep §2.2.3 (four timestamps on two timelines, p. 3), Are We Ready Table 3 (26.0 vs 11.7), Table 2 (Zep 44.4; Mem0 15.6 and Letta 17.8 below long context 20.0) and p. 10 (155.1 s, 116.5 s, 3.67 s), ForgetEval 17/242 = 7.0% (p. 9), MemoryAgentBench BM25 41.5. The counts of 42 agent papers and 10 benchmarks are right, and both HaluMem and Are We Ready do have MemTensor authors. Point 10 is counted for the 'how to do things, not facts about the user' statement; AWM itself is only listed. Point 22 is counted without the latency half. Not checked: that Mem0 and MemoryOS permute LoCoMo category labels, that re-runs of A-MEM and Mem0 come out much lower, and the reference to 'your own note on Zep'. It omits write-time loss (HaluMem), the store-size comparison and Zep's LongMemEval win over full context.

asis-q4-r2.review_only: that comparison rests on the review only, since I did not open those two tables.
asis-q4-r2.comment: Every number I checked matches: Mem0 p. 14 and Table 2, Zep Table 2, Are We Ready Table 2 (44.4 / 15.6 / 20.0), ForgetEval (7.0% and 9.5%, single author), HaluMem p. 11, and Fundamental Problems Table 4 (Generative Accuracy on downstream facts 0.97 before and 0.01 after the edit, §6.5). 7 papers carry page links. The one claim it flags as review-only also holds in the papers, roughly: MemOS's LoCoMo table has Zep 59.22 vs Mem0 64.57 (5.4 below, stated as 6), and MIRIX's has Zep 79.09 vs Mem0 62.47 (16.6 above). 'The corresponding author' of HaluMem is loose: there are two, one at Harbin Engineering University and one at MemTensor. The Memory in the Age citation (p. 29–31) supports text being inspectable and editable, not the hosted-API point. It also opens with 'checked the numbers below against the paper notes'. The bullet headed 'Cost moves between write time and read time' is really about store size, so point 14 is not counted. Points 4 and 5 are only gestured at; point 12 appears as a family, not an axis. It misses the functional split and most of the 12-system study.
